NASB.3: The chief was Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; and Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth, and Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite,
NASB.4: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty. Then Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Jozabad the Gederathite,
NASB.5: Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, Shephatiah the Haruphite,
NASB.6: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, Jashobeam, the Korahites,
NASB.7: and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.
NASB.8: From the Gadites there came over to David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear, and whose faces were like the faces of lions, and [they were] as swift as the gazelles on the mountains.
NASB.9: Ezer [was] the first, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
NASB.10: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
NASB.11: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
NASB.12: Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
NASB.13: Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
NASB.14: These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army; he who was least was equal to a hundred and the greatest to a thousand.
NASB.15: These are the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month when it was overflowing all its banks and they put to flight all those in the valleys, both to the east and to the west.
NASB.16: Then some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.
NASB.17: David went out to meet them, and said to them, 'If you come peacefully to me to help me, my heart shall be united with you; but if to betray me to my adversaries, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers look on [it] and decide.'
NASB.18: Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, who was the chief of the thirty, [and he said], '[We] are yours, O David, And with you, O son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, And peace to him who helps you; Indeed, your God helps you!' Then David received them and made them captains of the band.
NASB.19: From Manasseh also some defected to David when he was about to go to battle with the Philistines against Saul. But they did not help them, for the lords of the Philistines after consultation sent him away, saying, 'At [the cost of] our heads he may defect to his master Saul.'
NASB.20: As he went to Ziklag there defected to him from Manasseh: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu and Zillethai, captains of thousands who belonged to Manasseh.
NASB.21: They helped David against the band of raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor, and were captains in the army.
NASB.22: For day by day [men] came to David to help him, until there was a great army like the army of God.
NASB.23: Now these are the numbers of the divisions equipped for war, who came to David at Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of the LORD.
NASB.24: The sons of Judah who bore shield and spear [were] 6,800, equipped for war.
NASB.25: Of the sons of Simeon, mighty men of valor for war, 7,100.
NASB.27: Now Jehoiada was the leader of [the house of] Aaron, and with him were 3,700,
NASB.28: also Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father's house twenty-two captains.
NASB.29: Of the sons of Benjamin, Saul's kinsmen, 3,000; for until now the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.
NASB.30: Of the sons of Ephraim 20,800, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers' households.
NASB.31: Of the half-tribe of Manasseh 18,000, who were designated by name to come and make David king.
NASB.32: Of the sons of Issachar, men who understood the times, with knowledge of what Israel should do, their chiefs [were] two hundred; and all their kinsmen [were] at their command.
NASB.33: Of Zebulun, there were 50,000 who went out in the army, who could draw up in battle formation with all kinds of weapons of war and helped [David] with an undivided heart.
NASB.34: Of Naphtali [there were] 1,000 captains, and with them 37,000 with shield and spear.
NASB.35: Of the Danites who could draw up in battle formation, [there were] 28,600.
NASB.36: Of Asher [there were] 40,000 who went out in the army to draw up in battle formation.
NASB.37: From the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites and the Gadites and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, [there were] 120,000 with all [kinds] of weapons of war for the battle.
NASB.38: All these, being men of war who could draw up in battle formation, came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest also of Israel were of one mind to make David king.
NASB.39: They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had prepared for them.
NASB.40: Moreover those who were near to them, [even] as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules and on oxen, great quantities of flour cakes, fig cakes and bunches of raisins, wine, oil, oxen and sheep. There was joy indeed in Israel.

CSB17.6: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
CSB17.7: and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

CSB17.9: Ezer was the chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,
CSB17.14: These Gadites were army commanders; the least of them was a match for a hundred, and the greatest of them for a thousand. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.15: These are the men who crossed the Jordan in the first month <sup>[1]</sup> when it was overflowing all its banks, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and put to flight all those in the valleys to the east and to the west.
CSB17.16: Other Benjaminites and men from Judah also went to David at the stronghold. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.17: David went out to meet them and said to them, “If you have come in peace to help me, my heart will be united with you, but if you have come to betray me to my enemies even though my hands have done no wrong, may the God of our ancestors look on it and judge.”
CSB17.18:
Then the Spirit enveloped [2] ⓑ Amasai, ⓒ chief of the Thirty, and he said: We are yours, David,
we are with you, son of Jesse!
Peace, peace to you,
and peace to him who helps you, ⓓ

CSB17.20: When David went to Ziklag, some men from Manasseh defected to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of thousands in Manasseh.
CSB17.21: They helped David against the raiders, <sup>ⓕ</sup> for they were all valiant warriors and commanders in the army.
CSB17.22: At that time, men came day after day to help David until there was a great army, like an army of God. <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.23: The numbers of the armed troops who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul’s kingdom over to him, <sup>ⓗ</sup> according to the LORD’s word, <sup>ⓘ</sup> were as follows:
CSB17.24: From the Judahites: 6,800 armed troops bearing shields and spears.
CSB17.25: From the Simeonites: 7,100 valiant warriors ready for war.
CSB17.27: in addition to Jehoiada, leader of the house of Aaron, with 3,700 men;
CSB17.28: and Zadok, ⓙ a young valiant warrior, with 22 commanders from his father’s family. [4]
CSB17.29: From the Benjaminites, the relatives of Saul: ⓚ 3,000 (up to that time the majority of the Benjaminites maintained their allegiance to the house of Saul).
CSB17.30: From the Ephraimites: 20,800 valiant warriors who were famous men in their ancestral families. [5]
CSB17.31: From half the tribe of Manasseh: 18,000 designated by name to come and make David king.
CSB17.32: From the Issacharites, who understood the times ⓛ and knew what Israel should do: 200 chiefs with all their relatives under their command.
CSB17.33: From Zebulun: 50,000 who could serve in the army, trained for battle with all kinds of weapons of war, with one purpose ⓜ to help David. [6]

CSB17.35: From the Danites: 28,600 trained for battle.
CSB17.36: From Asher: 40,000 who could serve in the army, trained for battle.
CSB17.37: From across the Jordan — from the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh: 120,000 men equipped with all the military weapons of war.

CSB17.40: In addition, their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali came and brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen — abundant provisions of flour, fig cakes, raisins, wine and oil, herds, and flocks. <sup>ⓐ</sup> Indeed, there was joy in Israel.

NLT.1: The following men joined David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul son of Kish. They were among the warriors who fought beside David in battle.

NLT.3:
Their leader was Ahiezer son of Shemaah from Gibeah; his brother Joash was second-in-command. These were the other warriors: Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth;
Beracah;
Jehu from Anathoth;
NLT.4:
Ishmaiah from Gibeon, a famous warrior and leader among the Thirty;
Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederah;
NLT.5: Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah from Haruph;
NLT.6: Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, who were Korahites;
NLT.7: Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor.
NLT.8: Some brave and experienced warriors from the tribe of Gad also defected to David while he was at the stronghold in the wilderness. They were expert with both shield and spear, as fierce as lions and as swift as deer on the mountains.
NLT.9:
Ezer was their leader.
Obadiah was second.
Eliab was third.
NLT.14: These warriors from Gad were army commanders. The weakest among them could take on a hundred regular troops, and the strongest could take on a thousand!
NLT.15: These were the men who crossed the Jordan River during its seasonal flooding at the beginning of the year and drove out all the people living in the lowlands on both the east and west banks.
NLT.16: Others from Benjamin and Judah came to David at the stronghold.
NLT.17: David went out to meet them and said, “If you have come in peace to help me, we are friends. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies when I am innocent, then may the God of our ancestors see it and punish you.”
NLT.18:
Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, the leader of the Thirty, and he said, “We are yours, David!
We are on your side, son of Jesse.
Peace and prosperity be with you,
and success to all who help you,
for your God is the one who helps you.”
So David let them join him, and he made them officers over his troops.
NLT.19: Some men from Manasseh defected from the Israelite army and joined David when he set out with the Philistines to fight against Saul. But as it turned out, the Philistine rulers refused to let David and his men go with them. After much discussion, they sent them back, for they said, “It will cost us our heads if David switches loyalties to Saul and turns against us.”
NLT.20: Here is a list of the men from Manasseh who defected to David as he was returning to Ziklag: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai. Each commanded 1,000 troops from the tribe of Manasseh.
NLT.21: They helped David chase down bands of raiders, for they were all brave and able warriors who became commanders in his army.
NLT.22: Day after day more men joined David until he had a great army, like the army of God.
NLT.23: These are the numbers of armed warriors who joined David at Hebron. They were all eager to see David become king instead of Saul, just as the LORD had promised.
NLT.24: From the tribe of Judah, there were 6,800 warriors armed with shields and spears.
NLT.25: From the tribe of Simeon, there were 7,100 brave warriors.
NLT.26: From the tribe of Levi, there were 4,600 warriors.
NLT.27: This included Jehoiada, leader of the family of Aaron, who had 3,700 under his command.
NLT.28: This also included Zadok, a brave young warrior, with 22 members of his family who were all officers.
NLT.29: From the tribe of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives, there were 3,000 warriors. Most of the men from Benjamin had remained loyal to Saul until this time.
NLT.30: From the tribe of Ephraim, there were 20,800 brave warriors, each highly respected in his own clan.
NLT.31: From the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, 18,000 men were designated by name to help David become king.
NLT.32: From the tribe of Issachar, there were 200 leaders of the tribe with their relatives. All these men understood the signs of the times and knew the best course for Israel to take.
NLT.33: From the tribe of Zebulun, there were 50,000 skilled warriors. They were fully armed and prepared for battle and completely loyal to David.
NLT.34: From the tribe of Naphtali, there were 1,000 officers and 37,000 warriors armed with shields and spears.
NLT.35: From the tribe of Dan, there were 28,600 warriors, all prepared for battle.
NLT.36: From the tribe of Asher, there were 40,000 trained warriors, all prepared for battle.
NLT.37: From the east side of the Jordan River — where the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh lived — there were 120,000 troops armed with every kind of weapon.
NLT.38: All these men came in battle array to Hebron with the single purpose of making David the king over all Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel agreed that David should be their king.
NLT.39: They feasted and drank with David for three days, for preparations had been made by their relatives for their arrival.
NLT.40: And people from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. Vast supplies of flour, fig cakes, clusters of raisins, wine, olive oil, cattle, sheep, and goats were brought to the celebration. There was great joy throughout the land of Israel.
